findings.passage: Isaac said the number of documented cases of noncitizens voting “may seem small” but said there was no reliable way to measure the scope of it “because the current system doesn’t require documentation of citizenship.”
findings.note: Quoted by Votebeat at the House Elections Committee hearing on HB 5337. Isaac says noncitizen voting cases may look few, but the scope cannot be measured because the current system does not require documentation of citizenship. Only the phrase in quotation marks is her own wording; the rest is the outlet's paraphrase.

Lead author of HB 5337, proof of citizenship to register to vote with criminal offenses. Heard in House Elections Committee 2025-04-24; committee report sent to Calendars 2025-05-07 (date shown is that last action). Identical to SB 16.
Author of HB 2738, relating to acceptable forms of identification for voting. Referred to House Elections 2025-03-18 (date shown is the referral).
Author of HB 2739, requiring the address on an ID shown by a voter to match the address on the voter list. Left pending in committee 2025-04-17 (date shown is that action).
Author of HB 4475, relating to acceptance of a voter executing a declaration of reasonable impediment; providing a limitation. Left pending in committee 2025-04-17 (date shown is that action).
Lead author (first name on the author line) of HB 3137, captioned "Relating to prohibited local regulation with respect to a firearm or air gun." Filed 03/01/2023; signed by the Governor 06/11/2023.
